intro.text: This entry describes spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105), a form of male infertility due to defective spermatogenesis; the specific causal gene and supporting reports are not recalled here with sufficient confidence to be stated.

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) is a form of male infertility due to defective spermatogenesis.
checks.evidence_quote: Variants in the androglobin (ADGB) gene were identified in an infertile male characterized by asthenozoospermia.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes male infertility (asthenozoospermia) linked to ADGB variants. Abnormal spermatogenesis is reported only in Adgb-/- mice. It never mentions SPGF105 or a numbered disorder name.

paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) belongs to the numbered series of genetically defined forms of male infertility caused by impaired sperm production or impaired sperm structure or function. Affected men are infertile but otherwise generally healthy.

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) belongs to the numbered series of genetically defined forms of male infertility caused by impaired sperm production or impaired sperm structure or function.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing identifies ADGB as a novel causative gene for male infertility in humans: from motility to fertilization.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports a genetically defined form of male infertility involving defects in sperm structure and function. It does not mention the numbered SPGF series.

checks.claim: Men affected by spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) are infertile.
checks.evidence_quote: we reported the identification of bi-allelic deleterious variants of ADGB in three infertile men from unrelated families
checks.explanation: The affected men are described as infertile. The abstract does not use the label SPGF105, but the claim is about the same patients.

checks.claim: Apart from infertility, men affected by spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) are generally healthy.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract says nothing about the patient's general health or whether he had any features beyond infertility; any such detail would be in the full text, which was not supplied.

paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure is genetically heterogeneous. Many genetically distinct forms are catalogued in the SPGF series.

checks.evidence_quote: 男性不育症呈现高度异质性，主要包括精子数量减少（无精症或少精症）、精子活力降低（弱精症）或形态学缺陷（畸形精子症）
checks.explanation: The paper calls male infertility highly heterogeneous, says genetic factors account for 15-30% of cases and names several causal genes (SYCP3, CFAP43, SEPT12). It does not explicitly say spermatogenic failure is genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Many genetically distinct forms of spermatogenic failure are catalogued in the SPGF series.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not mention the SPGF series or how it catalogues distinct forms.
